items.prompt: Given a list of time ranges [start, end] in random order, combine every group of overlapping ranges and return the result.
items.why: Ranges + 'overlapping' + combine → Merge Intervals: sort by start, then extend the last kept interval. Sorting is only the first step, and nothing is being chosen or discarded as in greedy.

items.prompt: Given meeting times [start, end], return the minimum number of conference rooms so that no two overlapping meetings share a room.
items.why: 'How many intervals overlap at once' → Merge Intervals with a min-heap of end times. The heap holds running meetings, not the k largest of anything.

items.prompt: Two lists of closed intervals are each sorted and pairwise disjoint. Return their intersection.
items.why: The items are ranges and the question is overlap → Merge Intervals (intersect variant: [max starts, min ends], advance the one that ends first). It borrows the two-pointer move, but the logic is interval overlap.

items.prompt: Given intervals, return the minimum number you must remove so that the rest don't overlap.
items.why: 'Keep the most non-overlapping' is interval scheduling → Greedy: sort by END and keep each interval that starts after the last kept end. Merging by start answers a different question.

items.prompt: Given an array of positive integers and a target, return the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is at least the target.
items.why: 'Shortest contiguous subarray' with a monotone sum → Sliding Window. The window is a range of positions, not a list of given ranges to merge.

items.prompt: Given a sorted list of non-overlapping booking slots and one new booking, insert it and merge if needed, in O(n) time.
items.why: Sorted disjoint intervals + one new interval → three-phase sweep (before, overlapping, after). Binary search can find the position, but the merge still costs O(n).

items.prompt: Tasks have prerequisites such as 'task B can start only after task A is done'. Return a valid order to run all tasks.
items.why: 'X before Y' order constraints form a dependency graph → Topological Sort. There are no time ranges on a line to overlap.
